subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but solid module for a red panda standing on a mossy stone in a Genshin-style toon aesthetic, working out proportions like body length, height, and stone footprint to keep the scene balanced.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a hips root joint, a short spine chain running to the neck and head, and leg chains with hip-to-foot placements sized to match the stone's height so the feet land correctly on top. I'm working out bend directions for hind versus front legs and planning how the spine chain will drive the body mesh via a sweep with radius along a smoothed curve.

Writing coat shading logic...

I'm placing the head sphere, muzzle, nose, and jaw joint with specific offsets to build out the red panda's facial structure, keeping proportions small and layered forward from the head joint.

Now I'm adding the ears as flattened rust spheres with cream inner rims positioned slightly forward, then setting up eye decals using surface detection on the skull part to properly orient them on the head's curvature with mirrored left/right placement.

For cheek markings, I'm positioning cream patches at the sides of the face, carefully checking the coordinates against eye placement to avoid overlapping—working through the trigonometry of the eye's azimuth and elevation on the head sphere to make sure the cheek ruffs sit just below and outside the eyes rather than covering them.

Now I'm setting the head center position and eye azimuth, then moving to limbs: legs will be built as chain sweeps with dark brown coloring and tapered radii, with separate dark sphere paws at the foot tips, and a bushy ringed tail curving upward from the hips using a multi-point chain.

Writing tail sweep and stripe paint...

Now I'm setting up the tail bone chain parented to the hips with a "tail" role, and parenting the shoulders/legs to the spine and hips appropriately. For the stone prop I'm building a low-poly rock from a scaled icosahedron with a flat-shaded mossy paint.

Checking the math for where the panda's feet land on the rock's curved surface, I find they're floating above the stone no matter how I adjust the scale, so I'm switching to a flatter lathe/cylinder shape for the rock instead.

Switching to a 9-sided cylinder with a flat top for the stone base, plus moss lumps and a drip pattern painted by height and normal direction. I'll rig the stone to the hip bone so it stays rigid, and set the floor so the bottom sits at y=0, then recalculate the toe radius offset to get the feet resting correctly on top.

Now I'm working out joint positions: foot targets around y=0.285 with paw spheres scaled and centered to match, hip height at 0.43 giving enough leg reach, and hip/shoulder/foot coordinates for front and back legs plus a few spine points to shape the body curve.

I'm figuring out bend directions for elbows versus knees, naming convention with side suffixes for left/right symmetry, and adding ruff/cheek details like a rust neck sphere and small cream spots above the eyes while skipping whiskers and accessories. I'm also checking the color count stays under the limit before setting up the cheek geometry part.

Now I'm defining the lower jaw as a flattened cream sphere with its own bone and jaw joint linking to the head, then adding scattered moss lumps around the stone rim using flattened icosahedron shapes in a mossy green, skipping grass tufts and rune details, and wrapping up with the final export.

Writing the head joint and parenting it to the last spine joint, then adding an eye decal placed with a guarded lookup since the skin-around function could return null, targeting the skull part directly.
